item.title: Woman Who Accused Jay-Z of Rape Recants Her Account
item.description: An anonymous accuser’s retraction is now part of Jay-Z’s case against the lawyers who had represented her.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Jay-Z has been legally pursuing the lawyers who initially represented a woman who accused him of rape, but now says her claim was false. One lawsuit has been unsuccessful, but there is an open case in New York.

item.title: Cleveland Orchestra Players Walk Out, Forcing Cancellation of Performances
item.description: The strike, which began early Friday, is the latest labor action to unsettle classical music at a time of financial turmoil and uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nagourney
item.media:credit: Daniel Lozada for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cleveland Orchestra rehearsing at its home, Severance Hall. A high-profile European tour that was to begin next month is now in doubt.

item.title: Violinist Jennifer Koh on Her Decade-Long Struggle With a Rare Neurological Disorder
item.description: For 10 years Jennifer Koh struggled to understand and treat a rare neurological disorder, while trying to maintain a full calendar onstage.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Barone
item.media:credit: Tess Mayer for The New York Times

item.title: Weird Al Never Grew Up. Neither Did These Fans (or Their Dads).
item.description: Sons and fathers bond at the accordion-wielding pop parodist’s concerts.
item.dc:creator: Melena Ryzik and Timothy O’Connell
item.media:credit: Timothy O'Connell for The New York Times

item.title: Arthur Hancock III, Derby Breeder With a Flair for Bluegrass, Dies at 83
item.description: He raised more than one Kentucky Derby champion and wrote music recorded by the likes of Willie Nelson. He also spoke out against abuses in horse racing.
item.dc:creator: Joe Drape
item.category: National Museum of Racing and Hall of Fame

item.title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ and 9 More Songs to Hear
item.description: Taylor Swift offers sympathetic advice, Madonna and Charli XCX reminisce, U2 blasts garage-rock and more.
item.dc:creator: Jon Pareles
item.media:credit: Kena Betancur / AFP, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Taylor Swift’s “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” includes “Patient Zero” and three more new songs.

item.title: Pearl Jam’s Bass Player Is a Style Innovator
item.description: Fun hats. Layers. A blend of punk and jock fashions. A new book reveals Jeff Ament’s influence on a ’90s look that swept the nation.
item.dc:creator: Steven Kurutz

item.title: Jake Shears Loves a Scary Book. And Video Game. And Musical.
item.description: The Scissor Sisters frontman is now playing Frank-N-Furter in “The Rocky Horror Show.” It suits his taste for horror and spookiness.
item.dc:creator: Elisabeth Vincentelli

item.title: He Ran a Top Lady Gaga Fan Page. Then He Vanished.
item.description: Kirill Nguyen, the founder of Gaga Daily, said he had been imprisoned in Belarus for participating in pro-democracy protests. He resurfaced this week after an absence of more than two years.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado
item.media:description: Lady Gaga performing at Madison Square Garden in New York in August 2025.

item.title: Kennedy Center Shelved Repairs Now Cited for Closure, Whistle-Blowers Say
item.description: In a letter to Congress, former employees say the center delayed a plan to address the leaks that its officials now cite as a serious safety risk.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: Leaks in the roof overhangs of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts have long been a concern for center officials. But former employees say repairs were deferred as recently as this year.

item.title: Catherine Ringer, French Pop Icon of Eclectic Style, Dies at 68
item.description: With her guitarist-partner, Fred Chichin, she formed Les Rita Mitsouko as a band that embraced a more multicultural France.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nossiter
item.media:description: Catherine Ringer performing in 2007.

item.title: Review: With Dudamel and the Philharmonic, Joy Is in the Work
item.description: Gustavo Dudamel, settling in at the New York Philharmonic, led a world premiere by Tania León and Mahler’s Fifth Symphony.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Ferrari

item.title: Taylor Swift Named Her New Song ‘Patient Zero.’ Where Does the Term Originate?
item.description: “Patient zero” has long been associated with virus outbreaks and fictional health investigations. It was coined in the 1980s, by accident.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:credit: Nina Westervelt for The New York Times
item.media:description: Taylor Swift’s new single, “Patient Zero,” drops on Friday as part of an expanded version of an album she released nearly a year ago.

item.title: Sway Dasafo, Rapper Who Opened New Doors for Global Artists, Dies at 44
item.description: He won widespread acclaim as an unsigned artist, then used his fame to help other musicians in Britain and in Ghana break into the industry.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:description: Sway Dasafo in 2006. A year earlier, the cultural organization Mobo — an acronym for Music of Black Origin — named him best hip-hop artist, besting 50 Cent and other established acts.

item.title: Macklemore Announces ‘Free Palestine’ Concerts After Exiting Ed Sheeran Tour
item.description: The rapper, who was pulled from Ed Sheeran’s tour last week over his support for Palestinians, announced plans for three European dates.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Macklemore said that he had reached out to artists who have “used their stages to stand in solidarity with the Palestinian people, regardless of the consequences,” but did not announce acts who would join the tour.

item.title: Mayor Mamdani Becomes a New Advocate for Access to the Met Opera
item.description: The mayor, with a video filmed at the Metropolitan Opera House, joins the Met in announcing a program to distribute free tickets
item.dc:creator: Adam Nagourney
item.category: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts

item.title: Cheetah Chrome, Guitarist for Pioneering Punk Bands, Dies at 71
item.description: He played with Rocket From the Tombs and the Dead Boys, whose snarling nihilism opened the door to an entire music genre in the 1970s.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:description: Cheetah Chrome of the Dead Boys performing in 1978.

item.title: A Triumphant Baritone in a Dystopian ‘Macbeth’ Opens the Met Opera Season
item.description: Quinn Kelsey commandingly charts each step in Macbeth’s decline in Louisa Proske’s postapocalyptic setting of Verdi’s opera, which opened the Metropolitan Opera’s season.
item.dc:creator: Oussama Zahr
item.media:description: Lise Davidsen and Quinn Kelsey as the Macbeths.

item.title: Met Opera’s New Season Opens With Verdi’s ‘Macbeth’
item.description: Luminaries gathered to celebrate the Metropolitan Opera’s new season, which opened with Verdi’s “Macbeth.”
item.dc:creator: Sarah Bahr and Jutharat Pinyodoonyachet
item.category: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: From left, Keith Lieberthal, the lawyer married to Julianna Margulies, center, and Chelsea Handler.

item.title: Taylor Swift Announces ‘The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,’ Featuring 4 New Songs
item.description: “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,” featuring four new songs, will release on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Malia Mendez
item.media:description: Taylor Swift announced the new songs titled “Patient Zero,” “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

item.title: ‘It’s Very Simple’: 50 Years of Making Avant-Garde Music Sound Effortless
item.description: Founded by Pierre Boulez to treat new compositions with orchestral rigor, Ensemble Intercontemporain has honed the art of turning forbidding scores into expressive sound.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Arlo Brown
item.media:credit: Elliott Verdier for The New York Times

item.title: At 98, the Composer Thea Musgrave Is Still Learning
item.description: Musgrave, whose 1977 opera “Mary, Queen of Scots” is opening at the San Francisco Opera, has spent a long career searching for the “dramatic abstract.”
item.dc:creator: Hugh Morris
item.media:credit: Adali Schell for The New York Times

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Estate in Turmoil After Extortion Accusations
item.description: Ms. Parton’s manager requested a restraining order against her nephew and former security provider, accusing him of threats and intimidation.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane and Julia Jacobs
item.media:description: Dolly Parton’s death last month was announced by her nephew Bryan Seaver in a social media post.

item.title: A Back-to-School Playlist
item.description: Let tracks from the White Stripes, Madonna, Beyoncé and more transport you to the classroom.

item.title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Topples Mariah Carey’s Chart Record

item.title: Paris Really, Really Loves Céline Dion
item.description: Ms. Dion, the French Canadian diva, has embarked on her first solo tour of France since the pandemic. The French are swooning.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Porter, Giulia Imbert and Dmitry Kostyukov

item.title: With Helicopters and Dancing Camels, an Opera House Changes Its Groove
item.description: The Deutsche Oper Berlin is staging Karlheinz Stockhausen’s epic “Mittwoch aus Licht” at the start of a new season and a new era.
item.dc:creator: Ben Miller
item.media:credit: Katrin Streicher for The New York Times
item.media:description: Aviel Cahn, the Deutsche Oper director, wearing the new usher overshirt from the Berlin fashion and media brand 032c.

item.title: ‘A River Runs Through It’ Returns Home to Montana, as Opera
item.description: Opera Montana, a small company that has grown recently, presented its first world premiere, based on one of the state’s most beloved stories.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Barone
item.media:credit: John Stember for The New York Times

item.title: Soft Cell Finds an Ending Back Where It All Began
item.description: On “Danceteria,” releasing nearly a year after Dave Ball’s death, the synth-pop duo retreats into the grit and joy of downtown New York in the 1980s.
item.dc:creator: Jim Farber
item.media:credit: Kalpesh Lathigra for The New York Times
item.media:description: Though the album looks back on wilder times, Almond said he now finds the idea of club-hopping “completely abhorrent.” He added, “I don’t have the energy.”

item.title: At 92, the Bard of Bollywood Is Still Writing About Love
item.description: The poet and lyricist Gulzar has profoundly shaped the idea of tender romance in India through his verse and songs in more than 150 musicals.
item.dc:creator: Mujib Mashal
item.media:credit: Atul Loke for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gulzar at his home in Mumbai in July. He maintains the wonder that has fueled his work.

item.title: ‘Brothers’ and 7 More Things to Stream This Week
item.description: A series starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson airs. Three movies come to streaming.
item.dc:creator: Shivani Gonzalez
item.media:description: Matthew McConaughey, left, and Woody Harrelson in “Brothers.”

item.title: Louisa Proske Switches on the ‘Epic Brain’ to Direct ‘Macbeth’ at the Met
item.description: The rising director Louisa Proske makes her Metropolitan Opera debut with the season-opening “Macbeth,” a large-scale production that came with a ticking timer.
item.dc:creator: Elisabeth Vincentelli
item.media:credit: OK McCausland for The New York Times
item.media:description: “You dream of this as a young director, that opportunity to jump in and make something great kind of on the fly — on the fly in a large-scale, opera-time frame,” Louisa Proske said.

item.title: Ed Sheeran Addresses War in Gaza After Macklemore Is Dropped From Tour
item.description: Back onstage, Sheeran acknowledged “mistakes” over the departure of supporting acts, and discussed the “horrific” attack on Israel and the “humanitarian crisis” in Gaza.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Sheeran had no opening acts on Saturday and performed most of his set without a backing band.

item.title: With ‘Barely Breathing’, Duncan Sheik Became an Accidental Pop Star
item.description: Sheik’s song “Barely Breathing” spent 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in the late 1990s. But the success only propelled him closer to Broadway.
item.dc:creator: Rob Tannenbaum
item.media:description: Duncan Sheik performing in 1997. One critic at the time praised his “sensitive, articulate studies of relationships.”
